title: ToolImplementation
description: Normative shape of what a connector adapter or an internal module hands the wrapping factory, for agent/contracts/tool-wrapping@0.1.0. It is the registration surface, not a runtime payload: a declaration that does not satisfy this file yields no tool at all, and the refusal lands at registration where a connector author sees it rather than at the first call where a user does. The executable member is deliberately absent from the file - a schema can describe what must be declared about a tool, not the function the factory closes over and keeps unreachable (INV-AG-02).

name.description: Unique across the tool set of one session.

origin.description: Where a tool came from. There is no third value, and no value meaning trusted: an internal tool is not exempt from the wrapper, it is merely cheap to put through it.

description.description: Shown to the model. Text only, with no capability of its own: nothing the model reads here grants anything, because the verdict is taken outside everything a model reads or writes.

parameters.description: The shape the engine validates a call against before the wrapper runs.

declarations.description: Everything the gate and recovery read about this tool. Read from the manifest, never from the arguments of a call. This is the block a writing tool must complete: principle IV forbids a write whose reversibility nobody declared.

reconciliation.description: What an interrupted call can say about itself. The vocabulary is owned by ledger/contracts/tool-reconciliation@0.1.0 and referenced rather than restated here; a declaration that is absent or unreadable makes recovery fall back rather than guess.

snapshot.description: How the state about to be changed is read before the change, so undo has something to replay against. A reversible write that cannot read its before state is refused (SNAPSHOT_UNREADABLE) rather than performed unrecoverably.

read_operation.description: A read tool the same origin declares.

target_path.description: Where in the arguments the object being changed is named.
